tool.title: Precheck a push
tool.description: Run, before a push leaves the machine, only the fast checks whose inputs the push changed: `lock:coherence:check` (agreement and freshness) and `mount:remote:check` for a change to `index.lock.json` or `index.config.json`, `check:workflow-pins` for a change under `.github/workflows/`, and the typecheck for a `.ts` change. Nothing runs when the push changed none of them, and the full tier never runs. It is git's `pre-push` hook (`scripts/git-hooks/pre-push`), installed by the session-start primer; the same command runs it by hand (as the hook it is `--git-hook <remote>`, with the pushed refs on stdin).

inputs.name: dry-run
inputs.description: Print the checks this push owes and why, running none.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: One line per check run (✓, ✗ or ?), then the red checks' output. Exit 0: every check passed, none was owed, or none could be judged here (no bun, `cat` runner or `node_modules`; a dirty tree; a check that exited 2 or ran past `CAT_PRECHECK_TIMEOUT`, 90 s), each said in one line. Exit 1: a check is red, and the push is refused.

selection.when: Every push: the hook runs it. By hand before pushing a lock, workflow or TypeScript change, to see in seconds what CI would fail on, since every red CI run emails the owner (owner, card 2026-11-18).
selection.limits: Only the checks the push's own changes can break; it is a floor, not `gates`. It judges the working tree, so it judges nothing when the pushed commit is not HEAD or tracked files differ from it. `git push --no-verify` skips it; `CAT_PRECHECK=0` turns it off.
selection.cost: 15–60 s when a check is owed; nothing otherwise.

remedies.none: Without github.com, `lock:coherence:check` cannot read the pinned layers' mains for freshness and exits 2, which the precheck reports as not determined and lets the push through; the workflow-pins check and the typecheck still run.
